source_text: Cum ergo superius id egisset, ut intellegeremus a consortio iustitiae non potuisse excludi gentes, sed per eamdem fidem cum filiis circumcisionis in Abrahae stirpe numerari, nunc intulit neminem de circumcisione ad eam promissionem, quae Abrahae data est, pertinere; hoc autem omnino nisi intellegatur, repugnat. Quod itaque ait: Si enim qui sunt ex lege, haeredes sunt, evacuata est fides et destructa est promissio [n222] , non hoc pronuntiavit, ut videlicet nemo de Iudaeis per fidem fieri credatur haeres promissionis antiquae, sed deest sermo, cuius vicem implet intellegentia, non solos haeredes esse, qui ex lege sunt, ut si hoc modo dictum esset: Si enim qui sunt ex lege, soli haeredes sunt, evacuata est fides. Vere enim praeputium videretur excludi, si ad nullos praeter eos, qui ex circumcisione erant, benedictionis haereditas perveniret. Intellegenda igitur consuetudo Scripturarum est, quia non continuo, quod non dicitur, denegatur, ut intellegentiae opere verborum dispendia suppleantur.
pass_a_gloss: When therefore above he had done this, that we understand that the nations could not have been excluded from a consortium of justice, but through the same faith with the sons of circumcision be numbered in Abraham's stock, now he brought in that no one from circumcision belongs to that promise which was given to Abraham; but this altogether unless it is understood is repugnant. What therefore he says: For if those who are from the law are heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise has been destroyed, he did not pronounce this, namely that no one from the Jews is believed to become an heir of the ancient promise through faith, but a speech is lacking, whose turn understanding fills, that not only those are heirs who are from the law, as if it had been said in this way: For if those who are from the law are heirs alone, faith has been emptied. For truly the foreskin would seem to be excluded, if the inheritance of blessing arrived at none besides those who were from circumcision. The custom of the Scriptures is therefore to be understood, because not continuously what is not said is denied, so that by the work of understanding the losses of words may be supplied.
pass_b_english: Earlier, then, he had worked to make us understand that the Gentiles could not be excluded from the fellowship of righteousness, but through the same faith are counted in Abraham’s family with the children of circumcision. Now he has added that none of the circumcised belongs to the promise given to Abraham. Unless properly understood, this is a complete contradiction. Therefore, when he says, ‘For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is emptied and the promise destroyed’ (Romans 4:14), he did not declare that no Jew can be believed to become an heir of the ancient promise through faith. Rather, a word is missing, whose place understanding supplies: those of the law are not the only heirs. It is as though he had said, ‘For if those who are of the law alone are heirs, faith is emptied.’ The uncircumcised would indeed seem excluded if the inheritance of blessing reached none beyond the circumcised. We must therefore understand scriptural usage: what is not said is not automatically denied. Understanding must supply what the words leave out.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)
